newsitem.title: GERMANY: Higher MAN dividend not assured, outlook good.
newsitem.headline: Higher MAN dividend not assured, outlook good.

text.p: German truck and machinery maker MAN AG should see its business develop positively in the 1996/97 business year but a higher dividend was not yet assured, chairman Klaus Goette said on Tuesday.
Speaking at the company's annual general meeting, Goette said, "Positive developments at MAN are continuing and another good result should be made."
He said that if the economy continued to grow, MAN's earnings power should increase in the year which ends June 30.
In the 1995/96 business year MAN reported a group net profit of 330 million marks, a 21 percent increase from the year before. Sales climbed to 20.27 billion marks from 18.60 billion marks.
But Goette warned that solid results were not assured and that investors should not necessarily count on a higher dividend.
Goette, who is stepping down as chairman, said one should not assume that the dividend would be increased as a "good-bye" gift and that a higher dividend depended on a good result.
In the 1995/96 business year, MAN paid a dividend of 12 marks, up from 9.50 marks a year earlier.

The company also reported that group sales between July and November climbed two percent from the year ago period to 6.96 billion marks. Incoming orders, meanwhile, advanced six percent to 9.10 billion marks.

MAN shares slipped on the announcement, discouraged by the suggestion that a higher dividend may not be paid, falling five marks to 368 marks. Meanwhile, the broader German share market was firmer, with the 30-share DAX index up over one percent at 2,888.14 points.
MAN is heavily dependent on wider economic trends and has seen its truck unit, MAN Nutzfahrzeuge AG, hurt by a Europe-wide downturn in the market for heavy trucks.
But Goette said the outlook for trucks had improved recently and that if business continued as it had, "One would no longer have to speak about weaker markets of a year ago."
MAN Nutzfahrzeuge reported a pre-tax profit of 261 million marks in 1995/96, up from 209 million marks the year before.
MAN's other major unit, printing machine firm MAN Roland AG, announced earlier this month that it should be able to report a smaller loss in 1996/97 than it did a year ago.
Chairman Peter Bruett said that a more secure order situation in rotary-printing equipment should help the firm's earnings.
MAN Roland reported a group net loss of 81 million marks for 1995/96, less than a 145.7 million mark loss the year before.
